question: Who competes with BSP for home-services deals?
html:
BSP's main rivals for home-services deals are national HVAC/plumbing consolidators and four sponsor-backed buyers active in Punctual Pros' Central PA/NJ counties. The scaled players with cheap debt set add-on prices, while several leveraged rivals are more likely to sell assets than to bid.

National consolidators set pricing

Residential services is the most crowded field BSP plays in. These national consolidators set add-on pricing (Private-equity landscape):

  • Apex (Alpine)
  • Wrench (LGP)
  • TurnPoint (OMERS)
  • Redwood (Altas)
  • Any Hour (Knox Lane)
  • T3 (Riverside)

Their financing is uneven (Competitor filings):

  • Scaled tier: Wrench, Apex, Redwood and Legacy borrow at S+425–475, are marked at par, and have delayed-draw lines for acquisitions.
  • Next tier: TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour and Len the Plumber have moved to part-PIK interest and are marked at 89–94.

Local rivals in PA/NJ

RivalSponsorPosition
Sila (King of Prussia)Goldman SachsBuying near Punctual Pros; est. $450–650M revenue (low confidence)
Legacy Service Partners / HL BowmanGridiron (Fund V $2.1B)Buying near Punctual Pros; scaled-tier debt
Ally ServicesWatchtowerBuying near Punctual Pros
NorthwindsTruArcBuying in or next to Punctual Pros' counties
Haller (Lancaster, 254 trucks)Not in contextHealthier local rival

Sources: Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings.

  • Sila grew from a single ~96-person company in its 2020 PPP record, so nearly all of its growth came from acquisitions (Competitor filings).
  • Horizon Services is the clearest stressed rival. It has at least $211M of first-lien debt at Blue Owl, pays 3.75% PIK, is marked at 92.5, and was lender-owned by 2026.
  • Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026.
  • Both Horizon and Heartland are more likely to sell assets or restructure than to bid aggressively (Competitor filings; Home-services company case studies).

Where BSP is outgunned

  • BSP's Fund I is about $335M (Form D). Rival flagships run $0.9–2.1B (Private-equity landscape).
  • BSP should not join auctions. Its edges are:
  • the franchise-system angle: Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion
  • proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA that large-cap sponsors skip

Gaps in the data

  • Add-on multiples: The context has no add-on prices paid by Sila, Legacy, Ally or Northwinds. Deal announcements or lender reports would answer this.
  • Haller: Its ownership and capital structure are not in the context.
  • Win/loss record: There is no record of which rivals Punctual Pros has lost deals to. Deal-pipeline records would show the real competitive set.

Next actions

  1. Build a proprietary target list of sub-$3M EBITDA HVAC/plumbing shops in Punctual Pros' counties, ranked by fit for brand conversion.
  2. Monitor Horizon and Heartland for branch or asset sales ahead of the Dec 15, 2026 maturity, and prepare a carve-out diligence checklist.
  3. Track add-on announcements by Sila, Legacy/HL Bowman, Ally and Northwinds to build a local pricing benchmark.
  4. Confirm Haller's ownership and whether it is likely to buy or sell.
